taskCounts.title: Task counts: in columns and in the filter
taskCounts.item1: A column's header counter now shows not just its own cards but the total including subtasks at every level — `3 (6)`: cards before the brackets, the full total inside. With no subtasks the brackets are dropped; hovering explains both numbers (the same tooltip on a collapsed column).
taskCounts.item2: The filter row gained a `shown: 2 (4)` readout — how many tasks are visible right now, subtasks included. It counts the filtered tasks and is shared across every layout (board, list, calendar, timeline, Gantt, matrix); when grouping by tags, a task with two tags is counted once.

pageLayout.title: Document page setup and sections
pageLayout.item1: The document editor toolbar gained a “Page setup” button: sheet size (A3/A4/A5/Letter/Legal), portrait or landscape orientation and margins. The geometry lives in the document itself — it survives copying, versions and restore, and a landscape sheet is drawn landscape. Importing `.docx`/`.odt` now takes the page size and orientation from the source file.
pageLayout.item2: Section breaks arrived: from that point on the document starts a new section with its own sheet size, orientation and margins — a landscape table no longer flips the whole document. Sections are visible right in the editor, and the three pickers edit the section the caret sits in.

helpDeepDive.title: A much bigger manual: boards, tasks, tags and milestones
helpDeepDive.item1: “Working with tasks” is no longer a catch-all: documents, notes, reminders, milestones and notifications are sections in their own right now, and boards got a section of their own. It holds six new articles — the board bar, columns, view setup, saved views, a walkthrough of every visualisation (list, calendar, timeline, Gantt, matrix) and the archive.
helpDeepDive.item2: Tasks are covered in depth too: the task window and the fields a card doesn't show, the description editor with its toolbar, attachments, mermaid diagrams and full-screen mode, threaded comments with mentions, every link type, task documents and the change history.
helpDeepDive.item3: There is a new article on tags — prefixes, colours, two-segment pills and the one catch: a tag in the task window is created with Enter. “Milestones” now covers managing them, and “Documents” was rewritten to be about the section itself: the tree, the table of contents, discussions, version history, approvals, import and export.
helpDeepDive.item4: The sign-in and sign-up screens gained an RU/EN switch, and on first visit the language follows your browser settings.

helpEnglish.title: The help centre in English
helpEnglish.item1: With the interface in English, help centre articles now open in English. An article that hasn't been translated yet stays in Russian, so nothing goes missing from the manual.
helpEnglish.item2: Screenshots follow the language of the article: an English article carries frames shot from the English interface — in the light theme, the dark one and on the phone.

changelogHistory.title: Change history on click
changelogHistory.item1: The version line in the bottom-right corner is now a button: click it to open the full change history — the same What's New cards, all of them.

i18n.title: English and Russian interface
i18n.item1: The app now has a language switch — English or Russian. Change it in Settings → Language; your choice is remembered on the device.
i18n.item2: Date and time formats and the first day of the week fall in behind the language, and can be set in Settings too.

helpCenter.title: Help centre
helpCenter.item1: A question-mark “Help” button now sits at the bottom of the sidebar, holding both the guided tour and the new help centre. The manual opens as a window over the board — with section navigation, search across every article and a table of contents — so you can read it without leaving your work.
helpCenter.item2: The “?” in the topbar and in the task window opens the article about the very screen in front of you. Help articles also turn up in the global search.
helpCenter.item3: The articles carry interface screenshots, and in the dark theme those are dark too.
helpCenter.spotlightBody: The question-mark button at the bottom of the sidebar: the guided tour and the help centre with search across every article.

tourDnd.title: The guide now shows drag and drop
tourDnd.item1: The Get Started guide gained hands-on steps: dragging a card between board columns and dragging a project into a tree group, with creating a project group in between. A step completes once the item has actually moved.
tourDnd.item2: While you drag, the hint and the dimming fade out so the arrow does not get in the way of aiming.

docxImport.title: Word import and a steadier session
docxImport.item1: Importing `.docx` keeps the formatting: text colours and sizes, horizontal rules, code blocks, table fills and borders. Colours from Word stay readable in the dark theme.
docxImport.item2: A brief drop of the server connection no longer throws you back to the login screen — the session restores itself.
docxImport.item3: The new-version notice appears right away, with no page reload.

getStarted.title: The Get Started walkthrough
getStarted.item1: New users get an interactive 12-step guide: from picking a workspace to creating a project, a board and a first task, then a tour of the board tools and the sections. You can restart it at any time — “Get started” at the bottom of the sidebar.
getStarted.item2: PDF preview in documents works again: the pdf.js worker is no longer blocked, and the overlapping render passes are gone.

versions.title: Service versions and self-update
versions.item1: Client and server versions are now visible in the bottom-right corner — hover to see the commit and the build date.
versions.item2: The app offers to update itself when a new version ships, with no manual reload.

gitlabGrouping.title: GitLab: grouping and subtask statuses
gitlabGrouping.item1: A task can be marked as grouped in GitLab, and the Subtasks tab shows each subtask's GitLab status with a link to the issue.

descriptionTab.title: Description in its own tab
descriptionTab.item1: In the side-panel layout the task description moved into the first tab — comments and subtasks are now a click closer.

mentionCards.title: Mention cards
mentionCards.item1: Hovering an {'@'}mention in a description or a comment shows the user's card: avatar, name, login and role.

commentThreads.title: Reply threads in comments
commentThreads.item1: Replies render as a thread under the comment — indented and collapsible; “Reply” pre-fills a mention of the author.

editor.title: A better description editor
editor.item1: A formatting toolbar: headings, lists, checkboxes, quotes, spoilers; brackets close themselves and lists continue on Enter.
editor.item2: A full-screen editor with live preview, and `#N` links to tasks and attachments right in the text.

documents.title: Documents and task layouts
documents.item1: The new Documents section (alpha): wiki pages with a block editor — nesting, autosave, a drag handle per block and a “/” menu.
documents.item2: A task layout of your choice: modal, full screen or right-hand panel (remembered per device).
documents.spotlightBody: Wiki pages and workspace documents are available right now.
